first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A guide to getting married in Portugal, split by region, with the legal steps for US, UK and Australian passports, and a button to talk to someone called a Wedded Advisor. It reads like a very thorough destination guide first and a planning firm second. I get that they will plan it, but not who 'they' are or what they actually do for us.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Pretty and specific. The quick answer about a civil process for foreign couples 'at least one month before the date' and 'Check the rules for your passport' tells me straight away this is not just mood boarding. The line 'for couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom, with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' is the first hint of a service, and one point of contact is what I want.
Too early. I have not decided you are on my shortlist yet, so I am not filling in a form in the hero.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip
attention_map.why: This is where I look for proof before I scroll anywhere near a form. If it is hidden or just repeats a brand name, I have nothing. No press, no faces, no numbers.

attention_map.quote: a ceremony in a Sintra national palace or park booked through Parques de Sintra, then a Douro day for guests
attention_map.why: This is the guest experience picture I want. The honesty about Monserrate scaffolding 'until Q1 2027' actually makes me trust the content more.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: Airport on every card is exactly what I need for guests flying from the US or UK. But there are no drive times, and 'Guests' is left out or says 'Ask your Wedded Advisor'. I want to know if a place is within two hours of an airport and if it holds 120 people.

attention_map.quote: Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be needed for state events, and events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: Nobody else would tell me this. Good to know, slightly alarming, and it makes me want a planner who manages that risk. The page does not say how they would.

attention_map.quote: visa-free short stays on Australian, US and UK passports
attention_map.why: Useful for guests, but I have already decided Portugal is on the list. I skim this.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: This is the kind of supplier cost detail I want. It is about the venues, though, not about what the planner charges.

attention_map.section: s5-plan (Marrying legally, US and UK tabs)
attention_map.quote: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI; you sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer
attention_map.why: Specific to my passport, with the official source named and 'checked October 2026'. This is better than most planner sites. It is also the part I could bookmark and use without hiring anyone.

attention_map.quote: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate
attention_map.why: If the figures are not signed off, I get a list of cost drivers I already know. The euro-with-exchange-rate note is fine for supplier costs, but there is no number at all.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, an on-the-day coordinator
attention_map.why: This is the weekend, not the service. It tells me what the event looks like, not what you do from month 1 to month 18: venue search, contracts, suppliers, guest travel, design, budget tracking.

attention_map.quote: hidden at launch: only 2 Portugal real weddings
attention_map.why: I check proof before the form. No Portugal weddings shown means I cannot see your work here. A generic Europe strip is not the same thing.

attention_map.quote: a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: I have to get on a call to find out how you charge. The firms I am comparing at least say flat fee or percentage. No named senior planner, no face, and the founder quote is removed. 'Wedded Advisor' sounds like a call-centre title, not a senior planner who is invested in us.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links make a high-end planning firm feel like a magazine. I would ignore this row.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: s6 lists what a weekend 'can include' and s1 promises 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend', but nothing describes the planning service itself: what you handle, what we handle, what is in and what is extra.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: The brand line says who you plan for, not why we should pick you. s10 'Why book through Wedded Concierge rather than the venue directly?' is limited to 'approved service facts only', so I expect something thin. Nothing addresses where the team is or how you cover Portugal.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Every region card shows 'Nearest airport (code)': LIS, FAO, OPO, FNC. No drive times anywhere ('No flight times', Douro distance not used, Comporta 'shows LIS with no drive time'). Only Lisbon might get 'many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the centre', which is from the centre, not the airport.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: Supplier side is decent: the venue charges box and 'ranges in euros; AUD, USD and GBP amounts vary with the exchange rate'. Your own fee: not answered, 'a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call'. And the cost figures may not show at all until sign-off.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'See Real Weddings in Portugal (HIDDEN AT LAUNCH)'. Nothing from Portugal is visible.

trust_signals_noticed: Legal rules split by US, UK and Australian passport, with official sources named
'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.'
Honest caveats: Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027, state-event cancellations at Queluz
Airport code on every region card
No Australia-only framing; US and UK are named next to Australia
turn_offs_noticed: Vague scope: weekend described, planning service not
No senior planner names or faces
No real weddings in Portugal visible
No fee structure without a call
Celebrity trending row feels like a magazine, not a planning firm

emotional_response.overall: Impressed by the research, unmoved by the firm.
emotional_response.detail: I come away trusting the facts more than I trust the people. Nothing tells me someone senior will care about our wedding the way I want them to. 'Wedded Advisor' plus a form is not 'emotionally invested'.

payload.decision_reason: The Portugal guide itself is excellent: legal steps for my passport, airports per region, venue charging quirks, palace rules. I would bookmark it. But my bar for enquiring is clear scope, proof and fee structure from a firm that feels senior, and this page gives me none of the three: no Portugal weddings, no named planner, and fees only 'on the first call'. Next to the other firms in my tabs that show their weddings and their team, I would not send the form today.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly this is the most useful Portugal page I have read on the legal stuff, and I'd send it to my fiance. But who are you? I can't see a single wedding you've done in Portugal, I don't know who our planner would be, and I have to get on a call to find out how you charge. 'One Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' sounds nice, but what does that person actually do? Saving the tab for the passport rules. Not enquiring yet.
